sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the difference between the peace in "great peace for those who love Your Torah" and the peace in "and abundant peace for your children," explaining that the former requires the prior service of prayer to draw peace to the scholars themselves.

translations.translation: However, it is still necessary to understand that this verse
("Great peace for those who love Your Torah")
comes
as a continuation and addition to what is stated,
"And all your children shall be taught of the L-rd, and great shall be the peace of your children,"
for seemingly, even the study of Torah of "your children taught of the L-rd" and "your children" is after the prior service of prayer,
since it is written of them "and great peace,"
and it is explained in the maamar that "great peace"
("great peace")
is specifically for "those who love Your Torah"
(who love the Torah from the aspect that it is Your Torah),
for this love is through the prior service of prayer
(as above, sections 1 and 2),
and what is the addition in "great peace for those who love Your Torah" over "and great peace of your children."
But the explanation is,
that our sages, of blessed memory, said
(on the verse "and great peace of your children")
"Do not read 'your children' (banayich) but rather 'your builders' (bonayich),"
and the explanation of "your builders" is as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"What are 'builders'? These are Torah scholars who engage in the building of the world."
And this is the difference between the two verses,
for in the verse "and great peace of your children," which speaks about the effect of Torah in the world
(that Torah scholars build the world through their engagement in Torah),
also the intention of "and great peace of your children" is
(primarily)
regarding the peace that is made in the world
through engagement in Torah,
for the Torah was given
to make peace in the world.
And in the verse "great peace for those who love Your Torah," it adds that the great peace is drawn also to the Torah scholars themselves
("for those who love Your Torah").
And this is why specifically in this verse it says "for those who love Your Torah"
(that the love for Torah is from the aspect of the Giver of the Torah,
which is accomplished through the prior service of prayer),
because in order to draw an abundance of peace in the world, the prior service of prayer is not necessary,
but in order for great peace to be drawn to the Torah scholars themselves, this drawing is specifically through the service of prayer.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the work of tzaddikim and Torah scholars in building the world involves drawing the Ten Commandments, which encompass the entire Torah, into the Ten Utterances through which the world was created, adding a greater light than at the initial creation.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the maamar
(the discourse "Shalom Rav" 5704)
regarding the service of the tzaddikim who sustain the world that was created with Ten Utterances
[for this is also the matter of "Torah scholars who engage in the building of the world"],
that the Ten Utterances with which the world was created correspond to the Ten Commandments,
and as it is stated,
"Ten, ten for each shekel of the holy shekel,"
and that which Torah scholars build the world is that they draw the Ten Commandments
[in which the entire Torah is included,
including also what a veteran student will innovate in the future]
into the Ten Utterances with which the world was created.
And although even at the beginning of creation, the world was created in its fullness
(meaning that through the Ten Utterances there is a revelation of G-dliness in the world),
nevertheless, the intention of creation is that man, through his service, should draw additional light into the world,
even to a light that is above the source of created beings,
and this drawing is specifically through the Torah
(the Ten Commandments).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Torah scholars "increase peace in the world" not merely by negating the effects of sin, but by drawing from the Essence of the Ein Sof, thereby fulfilling the ultimate purpose of a dwelling place for G-d in the lower worlds.

translations.translation: And this is "Torah scholars increase peace in the world"
(specifically "increase"),
for the peace in the world that is made by the Torah scholars is not only the negation of undesirable matters
(the opposite of peace)
that was caused by sins,
that is, that the world should be in its fullness as it was at the beginning of creation
[and even to the extent that due to their great level
(that they are "your children taught of the L-rd")
they do not need special service for this,
for sin and the concealment of the world caused by sin does not exist for them
(relative to them),
and they see the world as it is in its fullness as it was before the sin],
but beyond this,
they "increase peace in the world,"
"and great peace of your children,"
(similar to)
the increase of peace that will be in the future to come,
because through their engagement in Torah they draw from the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above the source of the worlds,
and through this they complete the intention of "He desired"
that the Holy One, blessed be He, should have a dwelling place in the lower worlds.
